analyst_view.overall: Promoted Racing (12th, 14 pts, most of them at home) host in-form Real Sociedad (5th, 22 pts) at El Sardinero on Sunday afternoon; only Real Madrid have won there this season, and Racing won 2-1 at Málaga last time out. Racing miss Mantilla, Andrés Martín and Maguette Gueye (all in the numbers), Aaron Martín is a doubt, and top scorer Zabiri skipped a session but is expected to play. Real Sociedad miss Barrenetxea and Odriozola, and Yangel Herrera won't travel with a calf injury (all in the numbers); Mamadou Sarr, whom the numbers count as out, has trained with the group and one agency report even has him starting. Kubo, Óskarsson and Oyarzabal all scored for their countries and are back, with Crystal Palace away in Europe on Thursday. Manuel Orellana referees, already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals and already take off Barrenetxea, Herrera, Andrés Martín and Gueye. This morning I leaned slightly up because Racing's games are open and I had Herrera back; he is in fact out, as the numbers assume, and Sarr's possible return at centre-back would tighten Real Sociedad, so I drop the lean and stay at 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.3 corners, already trimmed for Real Sociedad's lower recent corner count. Racing attack down the wings with Íñigo Vicente and Iker Luque, and Real Sociedad use Guedes and Kubo wide; nothing new changes that, so I keep 11.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards and already add Racing's high recent card count (18 in six) and Orellana's record. Neither side has anyone suspended and the game has no derby or table edge, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots and already add both sides' busy recent shooting (94 and 96 in six). Two open, attacking teams trading chances is what the numbers already show; Real Sociedad's late-returning internationals and Thursday's trip to Palace could bring some rotation, but that is too uncertain to size, so 31.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. Zabiri and Óskarsson, both scoring regularly, are expected to play despite Zabiri's missed session and Óskarsson's late return, as the numbers assume; no change, 10.4.
